Hon 'b le Rak esh Th ap liy al, J.
1. Mr. Rajesh Sharma, learned Standing Counsel for
the Union of I ndia/ petitioners.
2. The petitioner-Union of I ndia has preferred this
Writ Petition to assail the order dated 23.05.2023
passed by the Central Administrative Tribunal, Circuit
Bench at Nainital in OA No. 410/ 2021. By the
impugned order, the Original Application preferred by
the respondent, who is the widow of Late Dev Ram
Arya, has been allowed, and the m atter has been
remanded back to the petitioner to take a fresh look
into the matter on humanitarian grounds, and decide
the same within six months.
3. Late Shri Dev Ram Arya was working in the
Postal Department. Upon his transfer, it emerged that
there was shortage of cash to the tune of Rs.
3,02,423/ -. Upon the same being pointed out, he
made good the said amount, without any contest. On
the allegation that he had misappropriated the said
amount, an inquiry was initiated against him , following
which, he was dism issed from service after 38 years of
service. His departmental appeal was also rejected by
the Chief Post Master of the Uttarakhand Region.
4. Since the said Late Dev Ram Arya had passed
away, his widow challenged his dism issal from service
by preferring the Original Application. The Tribunal
found that punishment to be disproportionate,
considering the fact that Dev Ram Arya had refunded

the amount immediately, upon cash being found to be
less, and the fact that he had served for nearly 38
years with the petitioner. The Tribunal, therefore,
directed the petitioner to have a fresh look into the
matter on humanitarian grounds, and decide the same
within six months.
5. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner,
and we are of the view that the view taken the Tribunal
is fair, and does not call for interference by us in
exercise of our jurisdiction of judicial review. The
delinquent employee could have been subjected to a
lesser punishment, so as not to deny him, or his
widow, the pension, which he had earned for rendering
38 years of service. I n our view, ends of justice could
have been met by the petitioner by subjecting Dev
Ram Arya to the punishment of compulsory/ pre-mature retirement, instead of dismissal, as that would
have not only sent a clear message to Dev Ram Arya,
as well as others in the department, to maintain
discipline in the conduct of their duties, but also saved
the right of Dev Ram Arya to receive pension for 38
years' long service that he rendered, about which there
was no other complaint.
6. For the aforesaid reasons, we find no merit in the
present Writ Petition. The same is, accordingly,
dism issed.
7. Consequently, pending application(s), if any, also
stand disposed of, accordingly.

( Rak esh Th ap liy al, J.) ( Vip in San g h i, C.J.)
